title: Backgrounds of the leading US online slot games: the figures and readings behind documents/background-recommendations.md

request.words: send another agent to create recommendations section, focusing on "Game background , slot background , amount of elements of the background , contrast , saturation." To rank it, sorted by theo ranking where applicable.

sortRule: Ours: each game stands at its rank in the most recent edition of the report that ranks it in "Top Game Ranks - Slots" (by Theo Win Index). Games ranked in a newer edition come before games last ranked in an older one; inside an edition, by that rank. Ranks and indices are copied as the reports state them, re-read from the five rankings.json files on 27 Nov 2026 after ranks 26 to 50 of the September, October and November editions were added. Every edition lists ranks 1 to 50 (reports.<edition>.ranksTaken); a game outside them is not ranked in that edition.

Nov.title: Eilers-Fantini U.S. Online Game Performance Report, November 2026 edition
Nov.notes: Read from the page pictures: the ranking table is an image. Taken: the slot ranking, ranks 1 to 50 (pages 46 and 47). Not taken: the overall GGR ranking (page 44) and the new-slots ranking, which counted for nothing towards the leaders in the July and August editions; they stay in pages/ and source.pdf. The publisher states that its data is a sample and may not represent the whole market. Theo Win Index is the publisher's measure of a game's theoretical win per site against the average game.

method.screenshot: One real screenshot of the base game at rest per game, from the run's game-screens/ (named per game under measured.screenshot).

regions.gameBackground: Boxes chosen by eye on the background outside the reel board, clear of logo, prize plaques and buttons (measured.boxes.gameBackground).
regions.reelWindow: Small boxes chosen by eye on bare reel window between symbols (measured.boxes.reelWindowPatches).
regions.symbols: The centre half (50% of width and height) of every cell of the reel grid (measured.boxes.reelGrid, cols, rows, symbolCores). A core holds mostly symbol and some window where a symbol is thin.
regions.reelFieldInPlay: The whole reel grid, symbols and window together.

method.boxes: x0, y0, x1, y1 in pixels of the screenshot, origin top left.
method.brightness: Mean luma 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B on the stored (gamma-encoded) values, 0 to 1. Same formula as Games-AI-art tools/measure.py.
method.contrast: 95th minus 5th percentile of that luma inside the region, 0 to 1. Same as tools/measure.py. rmsContrast is its standard deviation.
method.saturation: Mean HSV saturation (max - min) / max, 0 to 1. Same as tools/measure.py.
method.between: WCAG-style ratio (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05) of the two regions' mean relative luminance (sRGB linearised, then 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B), brighter over darker. brightnessDifference and saturationDifference are first region minus second.
method.differsFromMeasurePy: tools/measure.py measures a whole art file reduced to 160 px and weighted by alpha; here every pixel of a crop of a screenshot is counted, with no alpha. The artFiles figures are copied from each run's art.json and follow tools/measure.py.
method.rounding: The document's tables show brightness, contrast and saturation to two decimals; this file holds three.

recommendations.instruction: Make the reel window the darkest, quietest part of the screen.
Separate the symbols from the window by about 4:1 in luminance, or by opposite hue.
Keep the game background darker than the symbols; under a bright scene, darken the window hard.
Five groups of elements at most, at the sides and the top.
One hue can be saturated to the top if it stays dark; several hues cannot.
For a feature mode, keep the composition and change the colour; paint a new scene only for the main bonus.
Use a see-through window only to show a feature object, and tint it dark.

recommendationsNote: Our inference from sixteen games; not findings about the market.
